coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Radiance
record.summary: Radiance is a Bosa Development condominium building of about 99 homes (DBI's permit says 98) at 325 China Basin Street, the first of Bosa's three Mission Bay condominium projects; DBI's new-construction permit for a nine-story building was filed in May 2005 and recorded complete in January 2010, the Assessor gives 2008 as the year built, and the San Francisco Chronicle (via SFGate) reported the homes on offer in March 2009.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8720018 (5,405 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. The lot is condominium-mapped: 99 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8720018 and 98 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (OpenStreetMap (way 1258086102, name=Radiance at Mission Bay, 325 China Basin St)); 100% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 83% of the lot.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 8720018 (mapped 2007-05-22; active); the earlier outline came from: OpenStreetMap (way 1258086102, name=Radiance at Mission Bay, 325 China Basin St)

costs.what: DBI permit 200505112126's revised construction cost (estimated cost $27,000,000) for the 9-story, 98-unit building at 325 China Basin St; a permit valuation, not a vetted development cost

changes.text: The only architect named in a source read is John Perkins Sr., Perkins & Co., in a 2009 San Francisco Chronicle article; no second source confirms it. For the later 435 China Basin tower, DBI's data gives both 319 units (original permit) and 329 units (a 2014 permit correcting the count).
Radiance now uses its Assessor lot lines.

Radiance's March 22, 2009 SFGate article is a report that the homes were on offer, so the timeline no longer treats it as the completion. The Assessor gives 2008 as year built and the city's permit was signed off complete on January 19, 2010. Press says 99 homes and the permit says 98.
Added a sourced dossier for Radiance.

The map notes said Radiance is 9 stories per two realtor sources; of the readable sources, SFGate describes a nine-story and a six-story building and OSM has 8 levels, so the notes were rewritten. The 'first homes' milestone moved from September 2008 to March 2009, the date of the SFGate article that reports it, and the December 2006 groundbreaking milestone was removed because no readable source dates it. The OSM tag citation was corrected to name=.

open_questions: No primary opening date: the Assessor's 2008 is a year; DBI's permit sign-off is 2010-01-19; the Chronicle article of March 22, 2009 is the earliest dated report read.

Phase question: SocketSite (July 2010) called a 318-unit 'Radiance West' the 'Phase Two' at 325 China Basin, while Bosa's own page names the later 16-storey towers 'Madrone' and DBI's 16-story, 319-unit permit is at 435 China Basin (completed 2014-11-12; a second DBI permit there, 201205170704, completed 2014-10-27, states 'to correct record and document unit count as 329 units', so DBI's own data gives both 319 and 329). This dossier covers only the 99-unit building; whether the map's footprint includes any of that later phase is not established by anything read.

Architect: the only source read that names one is the Chronicle article of March 22, 2009, whose sidebar lists 'Architect: John Perkins Sr., Perkins & Co.'; no second source confirms it, and a brokerage page naming an architect could not be opened.
Unit count 98 (DBI) versus 99 (press, architecture database, Assessor parcel count).
Bosa's own page lists 'Status Active 2005 - 2015' for all three Mission Bay buildings together and '693' units; it gives no Radiance-specific date or unit count.
No OCII design-review or commission item for the block was located.
